verdict.headline: Oil jumps on Iran strike reports and a Gulf tanker attack, sending yields back toward 2002 highs
verdict.label: Pre-market Thu: Dow futures -0.9%, S&P 500 futures -0.5%, Nasdaq 100 futures -0.7%; 10Y ~5.33% (+5 bp), 30Y ~5.70% (+4 bp); Brent ~$103.91 (+3.7%), WTI ~$91.41; October hike odds ~18%; BTC ~$82,340.
verdict.rationale_short:
What happened: Brent rose about 4% overnight to near $104, after Axios reported the military had been told to be ready for possible new strikes on Iran and UKMTO reported a tanker hit by projectiles 94 km north of Qatar, with more than 500,000 barrels a day of US Gulf output shut ahead of a hurricane. The ten-year yield rose about 5 basis points to 5.331% and the thirty-year about 4 to 5.702%, within 4 basis points of Wednesday's 2002-era highs. Fed Governor Waller said more hikes are needed but need not come at consecutive meetings, and October hike odds stayed near 18%. Stock futures fell 0.5-0.9%.

What it means: the decline in yields after Wednesday's strong ten-year auction has been mostly reversed by oil, not by the Fed, since short-rate expectations did not move. Last night's report said Brent above $102 on further attacks would bring the inflation input back behind the long end, and that happened within hours. Stocks are reacting more than on Wednesday morning.

What would change the picture: the $22 billion thirty-year auction at 1 p.m. — strong indirect demand would keep the explanation on inflation, while a weak sale and a close above 5.732% would add supply. A Brent move back under $100 would remove the input behind both days' yield highs; an S&P 500 close under 7,666.45 would show the index following yields lower. Note: news sites could not be opened from this run, so figures rest on search summaries of the cited sources, and the VIX was unavailable.
verdict.lede_short: Oil rose about 4% overnight to near $104 a barrel on reports the US military is readying options to strike Iran and a tanker attack inside the Gulf, and long-term Treasury yields climbed back toward Wednesday's 2002-era highs. Stock futures fell 0.5-0.9%, while Fed rate-hike odds for October did not move, so the pressure is coming from oil rather than the Fed. Today's $22 billion thirty-year sale is the test: a close above 5.732% would show buyers stepping back at these yields.

supporting_data.label: Brent rose 3.7% to $103.91 and WTI above $91.41 on stepped-up attacks on Hormuz tankers and more than 500,000 barrels a day of US Gulf output shut ahead of a hurricane — Wednesday's IEA-driven decline reversed in one night.
The ten-year yield rose more than 5 basis points to 5.331% and the thirty-year to 5.702% — both within 4 basis points of Wednesday's 2002-era highs, hours before the $22 billion thirty-year sale.

Axios reported the military was told to be ready for possible new strikes on Iran as Trump weighs timing, with US-Iran talks stalled — advisers reportedly favour waiting until after the midterms, so the risk is timing, not an order.
Fed Governor Waller said more hikes are needed but need not come at consecutive meetings — October hike odds held near 18%, so the rise in long yields did not come from the expected policy path.
Dow futures fell 0.9%, S&P 500 futures 0.5% and Nasdaq 100 futures 0.7% — a larger reaction than Wednesday morning's for a similar rise in yields.
PepsiCo beat on adjusted EPS of $2.34 and $25.27 billion of revenue but cut its core EPS growth outlook to 2.5-3.5% — North American weakness is outweighing the quarter.

watchlist_mentions.note: Up 2.3% premarket after Yorkville Ives initiated at Outperform with a $250 target, one of few AI names higher into a lower open.
Down 0.6% premarket with Broadcom and Micron as yields rose; no company-specific news.
Down 1.6% over 24 hours to about $82,340 on Crypto.com, a third day trading with rate-sensitive assets.

trade_setups.thesis: The thirty-year is back near 5.70%, just under Wednesday's 5.732% high, after oil rose about 4% overnight. The $22 billion auction tests whether Wednesday's strong ten-year demand extends to the longest bonds with oil higher.
trade_setups.entry: Thirty-year ~5.70%; Wednesday's 5.732% intraday high and the 5.644% 2002 high define the range.
trade_setups.invalidation: Indirect bidding near the ten-year's 80.3% keeps the move about inflation, not supply; a weak sale with a close above 5.732% adds supply on top of oil.

trade_setups.thesis: Brent reversed Wednesday's IEA-driven decline overnight on Iran strike-readiness reports, a tanker attack off Qatar and US Gulf hurricane shut-ins. It is now the main input behind the long-end yield highs.
trade_setups.invalidation: A settle above $105 keeps the ten-year pressing 5.365%; a move back under $100, from a sized IEA release on Oct 14-15 or a quieter Gulf, removes the input.
trade_setups.horizon: Through the IEA board meeting, Oct 14-15

trade_setups.thesis: The index closed 0.2% below its record while yields hit 2002 highs; futures point to a loss of about 0.5%, a larger reaction than Wednesday's.
trade_setups.invalidation: A close under 7,666.45 shows the large AI names no longer absorbing higher yields; holding above it through a 5.70% thirty-year shows the index still separating from bonds.
